paper_container: Decision Corpus + Predictor Benchmark + Audit Protocol
question: How many endpoint-edge incidence dimensions are represented by FOREAGENT's released comparison rows?

disclosure.disposition: All values are post-disclosure deterministic description and external validation of an audit quantity; none is a preregistered hypothesis test or confirmatory effect.

estimand.quantity: rank of an oriented endpoint-edge incidence matrix over the released undirected comparison graph
estimand.formula: For a graph with V vertices and C connected components, incidence rank over the reals is V-C; cycle-space dimension is E-V+C.
estimand.why_relevant: It reports the exact number of linear endpoint-potential contrast dimensions represented by the released edge rows and makes endpoint reuse visible.
estimand.why_not_effective_sample_size: Label noise, feature sharing, model class, optimization, task heterogeneity, and dependence across rows are not modeled by this graph identity.

interpretation_boundary.allowed: Report raw pair rows together with vertices, connected components, endpoint-incidence rank, cycle-space rows, degree reuse, task/run grouping, and clustering assumptions.
not_claimed: that only V-C labels are statistically independent
that FOREAGENT's reported model accuracy is invalid
that row inflation causes any observed accuracy
that our predictor is more accurate
algorithmic novelty for graph incidence rank
interpretation_boundary.external_validity_role: Shows that pair-row inflation is not unique to our sibling corpus and motivates a common benchmark reporting standard across MLE preference datasets.

related_primary_sources.note: InstructGPT explicitly treats all K-choose-2 comparisons from one ranking prompt as correlated and batches them as one element; this addendum reports a complementary exact graph-linear quantity rather than claiming that precedent.
